Now I have the full chain confirmed in `guava/src/com/google/common/cache/LocalCache.java` (Segment class, lines ~1866-3483).

When `Segment.get(...)` finds a live entry whose value is non-null, it calls `recordRead`, then:

1. **`Segment.get`** (LocalCache.java:2091) — finds the live entry, calls `scheduleRefresh`.
2. **`Segment.scheduleRefresh`** (:2361) — checks `map.refreshes()` and that `now - entry.getWriteTime() > map.refreshNanos`; if due, calls `refresh`.
3. **`Segment.refresh`** (:2387) — calls `insertLoadingValueReference`, then `loadAsync`.
4. **`Segment.insertLoadingValueReference`** (:2410) — under the segment lock, re-checks staleness, swaps in a `LoadingValueReference` so only one thread refreshes.
5. **`Segment.loadAsync`** (:2317) — calls `loadingValueReference.loadFuture(key, loader)` to invoke the `CacheLoader`, and attaches a listener that calls `getAndRecordStats` when the future completes.
6. **`Segment.getAndRecordStats`** (:2337) — awaits the loaded value, records load-success stats, then calls `storeLoadedValue`.
7. **`Segment.storeLoadedValue`** (:3143) — under the segment lock, installs the new value into the entry (`setValue`) and runs `evictEntries`, completing the refresh.

If the load is synchronous (completes immediately), `refresh` itself returns the new value directly from `getUninterruptibly(result)` instead of returning the stale one — but the storage still happens via the same `getAndRecordStats` → `storeLoadedValue` path (triggered synchronously through the listener on `directExecutor()`).

ANSWER: On a hit in Segment.get, the order is: get → scheduleRefresh → refresh → insertLoadingValueReference → loadAsync (which calls loadFuture to invoke the CacheLoader) → getAndRecordStats → storeLoadedValue (stores the new value into the entry).
